title: Earthquake Early Warning

alarm.title: Emergency Earthquake Early Warning (EEW)
alarm.jp_phrase: 緊急地震速報 (Kinkyū Jishin Sokuhō)
alarm.sound_description: A rapid, repeating 3-chord chime ('Ponyon, Ponyon') on TVs and phones, followed by spoken Japanese: 'Kinkyū Jishin Sokuhō desu. Tsuyoi yure ni keikai shite kudasai' (Emergency earthquake warning. Prepare for strong shaking).

steps: Drop, Cover, and Hold On immediately under a sturdy table or desk.
Protect your head and neck from falling objects.
If outdoors, move away from glass windows, brick walls, and power lines.
Do not rush outside; stay put until shaking stops.

title: Civil Protection Warning (J-Alert)

alarm.title: Armed Attack / Missile Launch Alert
alarm.jp_phrase: 国民保護情報 (Kokumin Hogo Jōhō)
alarm.sound_description: An intense, high-pitched wailing siren or repeating 2-tone buzzer, followed by spoken Japanese announcements: 'Missairu hassha' (Missile launch) or 'Kainai ni taikiken kōkū' (Air space entry).

steps: If outdoors, take shelter immediately inside a concrete building or underground subway/basement.
If indoors, stay away from windows, close curtains, and lie down in a room without windows.
Listen to local authorities for follow-up instructions.

title: Tsunami Warning

alarm.title: Major Tsunami / Tsunami Warning
alarm.jp_phrase: 大津波警報 (Ōtsunami Keihō) / 津波警報 (Tsunami Keihō)
alarm.sound_description: Continuous long undulating sirens (5-second tone, 6-second break, repeating) emitted from coastal loudspeakers, accompanied by loud voice announcements.

steps: Evacuate immediately to high ground or a designated Tsunami Evacuation Building.
Do not wait to see the water—tsunamis travel faster than a person can run.
Stay away from coastal areas and rivers until all warnings are officially lifted.

title: Municipal / Town Radio

alarm.title: Disaster Administration Radio
alarm.jp_phrase: 防災行政無線 (Bōsai Gyōsei Musen)
alarm.sound_description: A pleasant 4-note chime ('Do-Mi-Sol-Do') broadcast over neighborhood outdoor loudspeakers, followed by municipal announcements regarding weather warnings, evacuation advisories, or local safety updates.

steps: Listen closely for key Japanese keywords like 'Pinan' (Evacuation) or 'Keihō' (Warning).
If sound is muffled by weather or distance, check your municipal website or emergency app for the text transcript.
Follow local instructions regarding community shelter openings.
